data.content_ref: inline:{"claim": "Two conclusions are the same claim iff they support exactly the same set of actions in the system's current policy, where an action is any externally observable output or internal commitment.", "mechanism": "The system maintains a mapping from each conclusion to the set of actions it licenses. When two conclusions license identical action sets, they are merged into a single node, and the action set is stored once. The policy is periodically re-evaluated to detect changes.", "scope": {"covers": ["goal-oriented agents with discrete action spaces", "systems where conclusions are used to select actions"], "excludes": ["purely epistemic systems with no actions", "systems where conclusions serve explanatory or communicative roles"]}, "forbidden": [{"case": "Two conclusions that currently license the same actions but have different truth conditions lead to a merged belief that is later falsified, causing the system to simultaneously drop all licensed actions even though some might still be justified by the other original conclusion.", "eval": "program:action_justification_resilience_test"}, {"case": "A conclusion that licenses a dangerous action in a rare context is merged with a benign conclusion that licenses the same action in all contexts, causing the system to lose the contextual restriction and perform the dangerous action inappropriately.", "eval": "program:context_sensitivity_audit"}], "prose_notes": "This pragmatic criterion ignores semantic content and focuses solely on behavioral equivalence. It risks catastrophic generalization when the action space changes or when the system encounters novel situations where the merged conclusion's original context-sensitivity is lost."}
